title: Mock 3 · Core Concepts
blurb: Structure, disclosure and commission rules, plus index, carry, spreads and IRF basics.

questions.q: Under the SIF Sector Rotation Long-Short Fund strategy, what is the maximum number of sectors the fund can hold?
questions.explanation: Sector Rotation Long-Short: min 80% equity, max 4 sectors, shorts taken at sector level (all stocks of that sector), max 25% unhedged short.
hints: Wrong — 2 is the minimum number of sectors in the Sectoral Debt Long-Short strategy.
Correct — the strategy is limited to a maximum of 4 sectors.
Wrong — 5 exceeds the limit.
Wrong — a sector cap of 4 applies.

questions.q: How frequently may an AMC allow redemptions in the SIF hybrid strategies (Active Asset Allocator Long-Short and Hybrid Long-Short)?
options: Twice a week or any lesser frequency
questions.explanation: Redemption frequency: equity SIF — daily or less; debt SIF — weekly or less; hybrid SIF — twice a week or less.
hints: Wrong — daily or lesser applies to equity strategies.
Wrong — the rule is twice a week or less, not monthly only.
Correct — hybrid SIF strategies are interval schemes allowing up to two redemptions a week.
Wrong — they are interval schemes, not close-ended.

questions.q: What minimum proportion of the trustees of a mutual fund must be independent (not associated with the sponsor or AMC)?
questions.explanation: At least 2/3 of trustees must be independent; at least 50% of AMC directors must be non-associates.
hints: Wrong — 50% independence applies to the AMC board.
Wrong — one-third is too low.
Wrong — 75% is the unitholder majority to remove an AMC.
Correct — at least two-thirds of trustees must be independent.

questions.q: Which of the following is a SEBI requirement for an AMC offering an SIF?
options: Maintain a separate website or dedicated web page exclusively for the SIF
Use a separate, relaxed advertisement code for SIF
Show the mutual fund's brand in a larger font than the SIF brand
Use the same logo as the mutual fund permanently
questions.explanation: SIF branding rules: distinct name and logo, MF brand use allowed for 5 years, smaller-or-equal MF brand font, MF advertisement code applies, separate website/page.
hints: Correct — a separate website/web page keeps SIF offerings distinct from regular MFs.
Wrong — SIF must follow the MF advertisement guidelines.
Wrong — the MF brand font must be equal to or smaller than the SIF brand.
Wrong — SIF needs a distinct name and logo.

questions.q: How often must the Key Information Memorandum (KIM) be updated?
options: Once every financial year within 3 months
Only when there is a change in fundamental attributes
At least once every half-year, within one month from the end of the half-year
questions.explanation: KIM: at least half-yearly within one month of half-year end; SAI: by end of 3 months of each FY; SID: within one month of half-year end.
hints: Wrong — annual update within 3 months is the SAI rule.
Wrong — fundamental changes trigger addenda, but KIM also has a periodic update.
Wrong — monthly updating is not required.
Correct — KIM is updated half-yearly using data as of September and March.

questions.q: A distributor onboards a new woman investor (new PAN) who starts with a lump sum of ₹5 lakh and stays invested for over a year. What is the maximum additional commission payable for this onboarding?
questions.explanation: Additional commission: 1% of the first lump sum (if held ≥ 1 year) or 1% of first-year SIP, subject to a maximum of ₹2,000.
hints: Wrong — the 1% figure is capped at ₹2,000.
Correct — 1% of ₹5 lakh is ₹5,000, but it is capped at ₹2,000.
Wrong — not the prescribed amount.
Wrong — exceeds the cap.

questions.q: A scheme has investments worth ₹520 crore, receivables of ₹6 crore, accrued income of ₹4 crore and liabilities of ₹10 crore. Units outstanding are 40 crore. What is the NAV?
questions.explanation: NAV = (Investments + receivables + accrued income − liabilities) ÷ units = ₹13.00.
hints: Wrong — this ignores the liabilities.
Wrong — this subtracts receivables instead of adding them.
Wrong — not supported by the data.

questions.q: Can an AMC offer SIP, SWP and STP facilities in SIF investment strategies?
options: Yes, while ensuring compliance with the minimum investment threshold
No, SIF permits only lump-sum investments
Yes, and the ₹10 lakh threshold is waived for SIPs
questions.explanation: AMCs may offer SIP, SWP and STP in SIF strategies, ensuring compliance with the minimum investment threshold.
hints: Correct — systematic transactions are allowed but the ₹10 lakh threshold still applies.
Wrong — the workbook expressly allows systematic transactions.
Wrong — the threshold is not waived.
Wrong — SIP, SWP and STP are all permitted.

questions.q: If an AMC delays refund of NFO money beyond the stipulated time, it must pay investors interest at:
options: 12% per annum, charged to the scheme
15% per annum, borne by the AMC
questions.explanation: Delay in NFO refunds: interest at 15% p.a. for the period of delay, borne by the AMC.
hints: Wrong — the rate is 15% and it cannot be charged to the scheme.
Wrong — no such linkage is prescribed.
Correct — delayed NFO refunds carry 15% p.a. interest that cannot be charged to the scheme.
Wrong — interest is payable for the delay.

questions.q: A scheme with a beta of 1.3 is expected, on average, to:
options: Rise about 3% when the market rises 10%
Rise about 13% when the market rises 10%
Rise about 7.7% when the market rises 10%
questions.explanation: Beta > 1 = aggressive; beta < 1 = conservative; the market's beta is 1.
hints: Wrong — that would be beta of 0.3.
Correct — beta measures sensitivity to market moves: 1.3 × 10% = 13%.
Wrong — beta measures dependence on the market.
Wrong — that would be beta of about 0.77.

questions.q: Mutual fund schemes must benchmark their performance against which type of index?
options: Any index chosen by the distributor
questions.explanation: Total Return Index reflects price changes plus reinvested dividends; SEBI requires TRI-based benchmarking.
hints: Correct — TRI includes dividends, giving a like-for-like comparison with fund NAV.
Wrong — PRI ignores dividends and flatters the fund.
Wrong — there is no such rule.
Wrong — benchmarks are set by the AMC as per SEBI norms.

questions.q: The SEBI committee that recommended declaring derivatives as 'securities' was chaired by:
questions.explanation: L.C. Gupta Committee (set up 18 Nov 1996, report 17 Mar 1998) recommended derivatives be declared 'securities'.
hints: Wrong — the J.R. Varma group dealt with risk containment and margining.
Wrong — not the derivatives committee chair.
Wrong — not associated with this committee.
Correct — the 24-member L.C. Gupta committee (1996) reported in March 1998.

questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of OTC derivatives compared with exchange-traded derivatives?
options: A clearing corporation guarantees every trade through novation
Contracts are tailor-made and counterparty credit risk is managed by the individual parties
Contracts are fully standardised in lot size and expiry
Trades are executed on an anonymous screen-based auction
questions.explanation: OTC: customised, decentralised credit risk management, no formal centralised position limits, little disclosure; exchange-traded: standardised and CCP-guaranteed.
hints: Wrong — novation and trade guarantee are exchange features.
Correct — OTC deals are bilateral and customised, with decentralised credit risk.
Wrong — standardisation is an exchange-traded feature.
Wrong — anonymous order matching is an exchange feature.

questions.q: An index has a base market capitalisation of ₹2,000 crore with a base value of 1,000. If the current market capitalisation is ₹2,500 crore, the index value is:
questions.explanation: Index value = (Current M-cap ÷ Base M-cap) × Base value.
hints: Wrong — not supported by the formula.
Wrong — that inverts the ratio.
Wrong — that confuses market cap with index value.

questions.q: At the time of its introduction, a stock derivative contract must have a value of not less than:
questions.explanation: Stock derivatives: min ₹5 lakh, ₹5–10 lakh on review, lot multiple of 25 (min 50). Index: min ₹15 lakh, ₹15–20 lakh.
hints: Wrong — ₹15 lakh is the index derivative minimum.
Wrong — ₹2 lakh is the bond IRF lot.
Correct — stock derivatives start at ₹5 lakh and are kept within ₹5–10 lakh on review.
Wrong — ₹10 lakh is the upper end of the review band.

questions.q: A share trades at ₹500. Interest cost of carrying it for three months is ₹10 and an expected dividend in that period is ₹3. What is the fair futures price under the cost of carry model?
questions.explanation: Fair futures price = Spot + Cost of carry − Inflows = ₹507.
hints: Wrong — adds the dividend instead of subtracting it.
Wrong — ignores the dividend.
Wrong — subtracts carry instead of adding it.
Correct — Fair price = Spot + Cost of carry − Income = 500 + 10 − 3.

questions.q: If the volatility of the underlying increases sharply (other things unchanged), the premiums of calls and puts will:
questions.explanation: Higher volatility = higher premium for both calls and puts (positive vega for long options).
hints: Wrong — volatility and premium move together.
Correct — higher volatility raises the chance of finishing in-the-money for both.
Wrong — spot price changes move calls and puts in opposite directions, not volatility.
Wrong — not how volatility works.

questions.q: What is the maximum loss for the buyer of an option?
options: The margin deposited with the exchange
questions.explanation: Option buyer: loss limited to premium, potential profit large; seller: profit limited to premium, loss potentially unlimited.
hints: Correct — the buyer can let the option lapse, losing only the premium.
Wrong — unlimited loss is the writer's risk.
Wrong — the strike is not at risk for a buyer.
Wrong — option buyers do not deposit margin.

questions.q: Futures prices are rising while open interest is falling. This usually indicates:
questions.explanation: Price ↑ OI ↑ bullish; price ↑ OI ↓ short covering; price ↓ OI ↑ bearish; price ↓ OI ↓ long unwinding.
hints: Wrong — long build-up has rising price and rising OI.
Wrong — short build-up has falling price and rising OI.
Wrong — long unwinding has falling price and falling OI.
Correct — shorts closing out push prices up while OI drops.

questions.q: A trader buys a 1,000 strike call at ₹40 and sells a 1,050 strike call at ₹18 (same expiry). What is the maximum profit per unit?
questions.explanation: Bull call spread: max loss = net debit (22); max profit = strike difference − net debit = 28; BEP = 1,022.
hints: Wrong — 50 ignores the net premium paid.
Wrong — 22 is the net debit (maximum loss).
Correct — strike gap 50 − net debit 22 = 28.
Wrong — not supported by the trade.

questions.q: A bond with a 7.5% coupon trades at a clean price of ₹96. What is its current yield (approximately)?
questions.explanation: Current yield = coupon ÷ clean price. A discount bond has CY above its coupon rate.
hints: Wrong — that is the coupon rate.
Wrong — that multiplies instead of divides.
Wrong — not supported by the data.

questions.q: In a Forward Rate Agreement, the party that agrees to borrow at the fixed FRA rate:
options: Has a short position in interest rates
Has a long position in interest rates and gains if the benchmark rises above the FRA rate
Gains if the benchmark falls below the FRA rate
Must physically borrow the money on the settlement date
questions.explanation: FRA: borrower is long interest rate; if benchmark > FRA rate, the long receives the (discounted) difference.
hints: Wrong — the lender is short interest rates.
Correct — the borrower locks a rate and is compensated if market rates rise.
Wrong — falling rates make the borrower pay the difference.
Wrong — FRAs are usually cash-settled without actual borrowing.

questions.q: In overnight MIBOR futures, the value of one basis point per contract is:
questions.explanation: MIBOR futures: notional ₹5 crore for one month (30/365); 1 bp = ₹411; tick 0.25 bp = ₹102.75.
hints: Wrong — ₹102.75 is the tick value (a quarter basis point).
Wrong — ₹5 is the bond IRF tick value.
Wrong — not the basis-point value.

questions.q: The strike price interval for exchange-traded interest rate options on GOI securities is:
questions.explanation: Exchange IRO: strike interval ₹0.25; at least 8 ITM, 8 OTM and 1 near-the-money strikes.
hints: Correct — strikes are available at ₹99.50, 99.75, 100.00, etc.
Wrong — ₹0.0025 is the tick size.
Wrong — the interval is ₹0.25.
Wrong — the interval is ₹0.25.

questions.q: Why does a calendar spread position in GOI bond futures attract lower margin than an outright position?
options: It carries only the risk of change in spread between the two months, not full price risk
Calendar spreads are exempt from margins
The clearing corporation guarantees a profit on spreads
Both legs are settled by physical delivery
questions.explanation: In a calendar spread the trader has no outright underlying risk, only spread (basis) risk, hence lower margins.
hints: Correct — opposite positions in the same bond leave mainly basis/spread risk.
Wrong — margin is lower, not nil.
Wrong — no profit is guaranteed.
Wrong — IRFs are cash-settled.
